stem: When writing a conservative teaching summary on paediatric renal investigations, what is the best way to avoid unsupported overreach?

options.text: Limit the summary to explicitly listed tests and the statement that investigations are tailored to the individual
Add standard UTI imaging algorithms from memory
Use common exam-bank sequences if they sound familiar
Assume urine culture and imaging rules are implied by the heading UTI
Infer detailed interpretation rules from the table of contents alone

explanation: Limit the summary to explicitly listed tests and the statement that investigations are tailored to the individual. This stays within the supported material and avoids adding unlisted algorithms or assumptions.

citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because it keeps the summary faithful to the explicit content and preserves the principle that investigations are tailored to the individual.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because adding algorithms from memory introduces unsupported information not present in the source.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because familiarity with exam-bank patterns is not a valid basis for clinical content in a conservative summary.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a heading alone does not justify inferring specific urine culture or imaging rules.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the table of contents indicates topic coverage, not detailed investigation rules or interpretation guidance.
